I removed the swallowed error: `if (!done) await reader.cancel().catch(() => {})` is now `if (!finished) await reader.cancel()`, with no catch. `bun test` passes on its own after the last change: 10 pass, 0 fail.

The catch was hiding a real ordering problem, not an error that needed silencing. `finally` called `cancel()` even when a `read()` had already failed, and a stream that has errored rejects `cancel()`. I tested that in a probe, which I then deleted: `cancel()` rejects only after a read has already thrown, and succeeds on an open or closed stream. So the fix is to mark the stream `finished` when a read throws as well as when it ends, and only cancel streams that are still open. A consumer who breaks out early still gets the cancel, and any real cancel error now propagates instead of being hidden.

I did not change any tests.
